author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory, reachable by its address alone, lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name with the veterinarians holding it, each shown by full name, all on one page.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is requested, then every specialty is listed by its stored name on a single page with no pagination
given a specialty held by veterinarians, when the specialty directory is opened, then each holder is listed under it by first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary")
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on it
given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under each of them (PRD edge case 3)
given a specialty held by no veterinarian, when the specialty directory is opened, then the specialty is still listed with no veterinarian under it (PRD edge case 4)
given the specialty directory, when it is opened twice, then specialties and the veterinarians under each appear in the same stable order both times (PRD edge case 5)
given any other page of the system, when it is rendered, then it carries no navigation entry and no link to the specialty directory

given the specialty directory, when it is rendered, then it carries the shared navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory (REQ-SYS-001) and offers no way to change a specialty or a veterinarian
given the supported languages, when the wording is checked, then every piece of new page wording exists in every language and none is hard-coded (REQ-LANG-002)
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged per the owner)
Any navigation entry or link from another page to the specialty directory (owner deferred to a possible follow-up request)
Searching or filtering specialties or veterinarians (NG-9)
A machine-readable form of the specialty directory
Translating or reformatting stored specialty names
notes: No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. No autofix records to audit. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions, each decided narrowly for this slice: (1) visible entry point, deferred by the owner; (2) marking a specialty held by no veterinarian as 'none', not done, it is listed with nothing under it; (3) the specific order, only a stable order is required. REQ-LANG-002 is already covered by the existing i18n sync tests, which must stay green with the new wording. No new ubiquitous-language term: 'specialty directory' names a page, like 'veterinarian directory', not a domain concept.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only inverse view inside the vet package; no cross-package reference, no write path (NG-2 honoured). Three new types follow in-force patterns (system-design § Contracts, rows added with REQ-VET-003): SpecialtyRepository mirrors the PetTypeRepository precedent of a name-ordered lookup read, but extends Spring Data's plain Repository like VetRepository so it declares no write method; SpecialtyDirectory is a value object (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Value object) built by a pure static factory from the specialties plus VetRepository's cached full list; SpecialtyController is a Web controller that calls both repositories, hands the results to the factory, and renders vets/specialtyList. The grouping and ordering live in the value object, not the controller (Web controller row: no business rule). The adjustment is the new § Scale and Load section with its one row for this path. Covering symbols confirmed by grep (weaker basis, IDE oracle not connected): Vet.getSpecialties, VetRepository.findAll() @Cacheable("vets"), PetTypeRepository ORDER BY name, layout.html menuItem fragment.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html binds no request input: no request parameter, path variable, or model attribute, so there is no binding target and no persisted type is bound (security-principles trust boundaries; the page is output only).

Template vets/specialtyList.html uses fragments/layout with a menu value that matches no existing menu item. The shared navigation renders unchanged and gains no new entry, and no other template links to the route (PRD non-goal). Holders render as first name, space, last name, as vetList.html does. Specialty names render th:text-escaped, exactly as stored.

New page wording (heading, column labels) goes in messages.properties and every locale bundle; I18nPropertiesSyncTest must stay green (REQ-LANG-002). No wording marks an unheld specialty (PRD open question: nothing is listed under it).

Boundary repository, SpecialtyDirectory unit tests: no double at all. Build real Specialty and Vet instances (the framework-mapped entities are plain objects) and pass them to the pure factory. The edge cases live here: unheld specialty, multi-specialty vet, vet with no specialty, and the order tie-breaks.

Boundary repository, controller tests: the real repositories over seeded H2, via @SpringBootTest with @AutoConfigureMockMvc and MockMvc for the transport (testing-principles § Mocking Policy). The seed covers a vet holding several specialties and vets holding none. A @MockitoBean stub is not sanctioned for the new tests, because the real implementation fits.
Navigation test: render the pages that use the shared layout through MockMvc on the real application and assert none carries an href to /specialties.html.

patterns.description: name-ordered lookup-value read. The new repository adds identity as tie-break, because specialties.name has an index but no uniqueness constraint
read-only Spring Data Repository base; its cached findAll() supplies the veterinarians
layout usage, full-name rendering, message-key wording

risks.risk: Matching specialties across sessions: VetRepository.findAll() returns cached instances detached from an earlier session, so their Specialty objects are not the instances SpecialtyRepository returns. BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode.
risks.mitigation: Match holders to specialties by identifier (getId), never by object equality or Set membership. A unit test builds distinct Specialty instances that share an id to pin this down.

risks.risk: Stable order (PRD edge case 5): specialty names are not unique, and VetRepository.findAll() has no defined order.
risks.mitigation: Specialties are ordered by name, then id, in the repository query. Holders are ordered by last name, first name, then id inside SpecialtyDirectory. Both orders are total, so repeated renders match.

risks.risk: Path scales with the number of specialties and veterinarians (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty directory row: unrecorded, treated as bounded).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one specialty query, the cached vet list, one in-memory grouping pass, no pagination (PRD non-goal).

risks.risk: Value-object discipline: SpecialtyDirectory is not framework-instantiated, so the persistence-entity exception does not cover it (architecture-principles § Scoped exception).
risks.mitigation: Record types with defensively copied immutable lists and no setters. The factory is pure and does no I/O.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. No ADR: every choice follows an in-force pattern, and none constrains later slices beyond the current-state rows. docs/system-design.md writes: REQ-VET-003 added to the Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository; three new rows for SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory, and SpecialtyController; one invariant sentence (no write path for veterinarians or specialties); a new § Scale and Load section (from the doctor template) with the specialty-directory row. Open question for the owner, not blocking: the design doc had no § Scale and Load section before this slice, so this row is its first. Route and view names follow the request: /specialties.html and templates/vets/.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Input binding: SpecialtyController.java:38-39 `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")` / `String showSpecialtyDirectory(Model model)` binds no path variable, request parameter, @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody, so no mass-assignment or validation surface is added; it is GET-only with no write route

Query safety: SpecialtyRepository.java:36 is a static JPQL string `SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name, specialty.id` with no interpolation; the interface extends the marker `Repository` and declares no write method, and the read is `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`

Output escaping: specialtyList.html renders stored data only through `th:text` (line 18 `th:text="${listing.specialty.name}"`, line 20 `th:text="${holder.firstName + ' ' + holder.lastName}"`), which HTML-escapes; `grep -n -F -e 'utext' -r src/main/resources/templates` returns no hit, and the new template uses no `__${...}__` preprocessing (the grep hits are all in pre-existing templates). That matches how vetList.html and ownersList.html render names

Exposure: the page shows specialty names and vet first and last names, which /vets.html already exposes. No new data class crosses the boundary. Because the app has no authentication, the route is as open as every other route. That is the recorded posture in docs/system-design.md § Security Context, not something this change introduces

Resource bounds: the unpaged page is bounded by data the application cannot write (docs/system-design.md Scale and Load row added by this change). SpecialtyDirectory copies its lists defensively (List.copyOf) and keeps no shared mutable state, and the controller singleton holds only final repository references

Secrets and supply chain: a sweep of the diff's added lines for password|secret|token|apikey|credential found no hits. The 10 message bundles add only a plain `specialty=` label. build.gradle is unchanged. `./gradlew dependencies` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE and jackson-databind 3.1.5. author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Four test methods (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByItsStoredNameOnOnePage, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEachHolderByFullNameUnderTheirSpecialty, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldCarryTheSharedNavigationAndNoWayToChangeAnything, theNavigationShouldCarryNoEntryForTheSpecialtyDirectory) assert on response content via `content().string(containsString(...))`/`content().string(stringContainsInOrder(...))`/`content().string(not(...))`, i.e. Hamcrest matchers threaded through MockMvc's fluent API, rather than AssertJ (testing-principles.md § Assertions: 'Prefer assertion styles that produce chained, readable, self-documenting assertions'; § Agent Decision Checklist #3 'Fluent assertions: Using the preferred assertion style?'). No other test file in the suite uses this content().string(matcher) pattern (grep -F -e 'content().string' -- src/test confirms SpecialtyControllerTests.java is the only hit besides VetControllerTests.java's unrelated content().contentType(...) call), so this is not an established codebase convention the file inherits under consistent-with-codebase — it is a new style introduced by this slice. The same file's theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderIdenticallyWhenOpenedTwice already demonstrates the AssertJ-idiomatic alternative (extract getContentAsString() then assertThat(...).contains(...)/.doesNotContain(...)), so the fix is mechanical and the file is internally inconsistent as written.
findings.fix: In each of the four listed test methods, capture the response body once via mockMvc.perform(get(SPECIALTY_DIRECTORY)).andExpect(status().isOk()).andReturn().getResponse().getContentAsString() (as the idempotency test already does), then replace each content().string(matcher) expectation with an AssertJ assertion on that string: assertThat(body).contains(...), .doesNotContain(...), and for the ordered-substring checks a chained .contains(a) with indexOf-based ordering, or keep the Hamcrest stringContainsInOrder call but wrap it via assertThat(body).satisfies(a -> assertThat(a, stringContainsInOrder(...))) only if no direct AssertJ equivalent exists; prefer plain assertThat(body.indexOf(x)).isLessThan(body.indexOf(y)) chains to stay pure AssertJ.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Additive and contained in the vet package: three new types, one new template, one new message key per bundle, and doc rows. No existing Java file, the shared layout, the vet cache, or any sensitive path is edited.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do what the requirement says. It is a GET-only controller with no bound input and a static JPQL query ordered by name then id. Holders are grouped by specialty id rather than by object equality, which is correct for the cached vet list. Holders sort by last name, first name, then id, and output is escaped through th:text. I found no flipped condition or hidden behavior change.

test_adequacy.note: The value-object tests assert whole-directory equality for the cases that matter: multi-specialty holders, unheld specialties, excluded vets, id-based matching across distinct instances, and tie-break ordering. The controller tests run over seeded H2 and check real names in order, no pagination, and that the link is absent from ten other pages. Only a vet holding no specialty (e.g. James Carter) is not asserted absent at the HTTP level.
